correctness.rationale: Proof uses all four Kunz inequalities and checks the boundary F=3; the known leaf partition is exhaustively derived. Each of the four branch translations preserves those inequalities, keeps its uniquely maximal Apéry element and makes it effective. Branches are pairwise separated by Frobenius congruence or parity. The displayed fixed-F counts come from exact integer intervals. A quadratic count of admissible rectangles plus explicit outside points proves N>=3L+1, with equality only at F=3,5,7,9,10,11. The standalone VERIFY.py independently constructs actual semigroup members and minimal generators and checks 5093 leaves at all F=3..299 not divisible by four; these tests corroborate but do not replace the all-F proof.

value.rationale: Conjecture 41 in Casas–Madrid–Rosales explicitly concerns internal versus leaf counts at fixed multiplicity and Frobenius. This theorem settles all admissible F at multiplicity four with a sharper strict two-to-one surplus, an explicit invariant-preserving injection and equality characterization; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or normalization check. The earlier genus-preserving correspondence changes F and cannot supply this invariant-preserving structure.
